title: Built-in observability and evaluation hooks
summary: Agent Framework emits OpenTelemetry spans and metrics that follow the GenAI semantic conventions. You choose the exporter and whether prompts and tool arguments are recorded. Evaluation hooks score agents and workflows locally or with Foundry evaluators.
useIf: You must debug agent runs, attribute tokens and cost, trace across MCP and services, or gate releases on quality scores.
avoidIf: You plan to record raw prompts in production without a privacy and retention decision: content capture is off by default for a reason.

explain.md: **Spans.** `invoke_agent <name>` (top level), `chat <model>` and `execute_tool <function>`. **Metrics:** `gen_ai.client.operation.duration` and `gen_ai.client.token.usage` (histograms) plus `agent_framework.function.invocation.duration`. Workflows add spans such as `workflow.build`, `workflow.run` (Python) or `workflow.session` (.NET and Go), `executor.process {executor_id}`, `edge_group.process` and `message.send`, with attributes like `executor.id` and `edge_group.delivery_status` [[tr36]] [[tr37]]. The OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions carry status Development and moved to `open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai` on 2026-05-05, so attribute and metric names can change; which build emits which name is UNVERIFIED, so check your backend before building dashboards [[tr45]].

**Python.** Instrumentation has been **on by default since python-1.6.0 (2026-05-21)** but no exporter is installed: call `configure_otel_providers()` (reads standard `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` variables) or `ENABLE_CONSOLE_EXPORTERS=true`; with your own SDK call `enable_instrumentation(enable_sensitive_data=False)`. Variables: `ENABLE_INSTRUMENTATION` (default true), `ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA` (default **false**), `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` (default `agent_framework`). Sensitive data means prompts, responses, tool arguments and tool results. **.NET.** Spans appear only after you wrap the client or agent with `.AsBuilder().UseOpenTelemetry(sourceName, cfg => cfg.EnableSensitiveData = ...)`; the default source name is `Experimental.Microsoft.Agents.AI` and your tracer and meter providers must `AddSource` the same name. Instrument either the client or the agent, not both, or content is duplicated. The Harness instruments both layers for you (`OpenTelemetrySourceName`, `DisableOpenTelemetry`) [[tr36]].

**Trace context across MCP.** With an active span, Python injects W3C trace context into `params._meta` of `tools/call` for MCP sessions the agent process opens (`MCPStreamableHTTPTool`, `MCPStdioTool`, `MCPWebsocketTool`), but not for hosted or provider-managed MCP tools or Foundry toolboxes, because the provider makes the call. .NET behaviour is UNVERIFIED [[tr36]]. **Foundry** server-side tracing (GA for prompt and hosted agents) is a separate pipeline from this client-side telemetry; both can land in one Application Insights resource [[tr50]].

blocks.title: Enable telemetry
Evaluate an agent
Enable telemetry
blocks.code:
from agent_framework.observability import configure_otel_providers

configure_otel_providers(
    service_name='support-agent',
    otlp_endpoint='https://otel.example.com',
    otlp_protocol='http/protobuf',   # Langfuse needs HTTP, the default is grpc
)
# ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA stays false unless you set it deliberately

blocks.title: Evaluate an agent
blocks.code:
from agent_framework import evaluate_agent, LocalEvaluator, keyword_check, tool_called_check
from agent_framework.foundry import FoundryEvals

local = LocalEvaluator(keyword_check('weather'), tool_called_check('get_weather'))
foundry = FoundryEvals(project_client=project_client, model='gpt-4o',
                       evaluators=[FoundryEvals.RELEVANCE, FoundryEvals.COHERENCE])
results = await evaluate_agent(agent=my_agent,
    queries=['Weather in Seattle?', 'Plan a trip to Portland'],
    evaluators=[local, foundry], num_repetitions=3)
for r in results:
    r.raise_for_status()      # raises EvalNotPassedError on any failure

whereToUse: Per-run traces: see which tool or model call was slow or failed
Cost attribution: token metrics by agent, model and tenant (low-cardinality dimensions)
Cross-service tracing from agent through MCP servers into backend services
CI quality gates: run `evaluate_agent` or `evaluate_workflow` with repetitions on a fixed query set
Local development with the Aspire Dashboard (OTLP 4317, UI 18888)

use: Always enable metadata telemetry in production; it contains no prompts by default
Record content only in development, or store it externally with references on spans, as the OTel guidance recommends for production
Run local evaluators in CI for cheap checks and Foundry evaluators for judged quality
avoid: Turning on `ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA` in production without retention and access controls
Instrumenting both the chat client and the agent in .NET with content on
Building dashboards on metric names without checking what your build emits
flips: Langfuse or another HTTP-only OTLP backend: set the exporter protocol to HTTP, since the Python default is gRPC
You need whole-trace debugging: sample traces with care, because metrics are not sampled but traces are

pitfalls.cause: The client or agent was never wrapped with `UseOpenTelemetry`, or `AddSource` used a different name than the default `Experimental.Microsoft.Agents.AI`
pitfalls.fix: Wrap once and match the source name in tracer and meter providers

pitfalls.cause: Both client and agent were instrumented with sensitive data on

pitfalls.symptom: Traces stop at the agent for a hosted MCP tool
pitfalls.cause: The provider issues `tools/call`, so no `_meta` context is injected
pitfalls.fix: Use a client-opened MCP transport when end-to-end tracing is required

pitfalls.symptom: Load tests look incomplete in Application Insights
pitfalls.cause: The distro samples at a default rate-limited 5 traces per second [[tr53]]
pitfalls.fix: Set fixed-ratio or lift the rate for the test; alert from metrics, which are not sampled

scenarios.title: Debug a slow agent without storing prompts
scenarios.situation: Users complain some runs take 40 seconds. Privacy rules forbid storing prompts and answers in telemetry. Traces go to Application Insights.
unknowns: Is the time in model calls, tools or approvals?
Is sampling dropping the slow traces?
scenarios.question: How do you instrument?

options.name: Metadata-only telemetry (default), look at `invoke_agent`, `chat` and `execute_tool` span durations and counts, with sampling tuned to keep slow traces
options.why: Spans show where time goes with no content, matching the default of no sensitive data.
options.tradeoff: You cannot see why the model chose a tool; add external content storage with references if allowed.

options.name: Turn on sensitive data in production to see prompts
options.why: Violates the privacy rule and exposes tool arguments and results.

options.name: Add custom logs of every prompt to a database
options.why: Same privacy problem and more code.
options.tradeoff: Only with consent and retention controls.

flips.if: Debugging needs content and rules permit it with controls
flips.then: Store content in a separate access-controlled store and put references on spans.
Use tail sampling in a collector, or raise the rate for error and slow traces.

scenarios.takeaway: Structure and timing are enough for most latency bugs; content is a separate decision.

scenarios.title: Release gate for prompt changes
scenarios.situation: A team changes prompts weekly and wants a gate in CI. They have 60 test queries with expected tool calls. Judged quality must also be checked before major releases. Runs are non-deterministic.
unknowns: Is a Foundry project available in CI?
scenarios.question: What do you wire into CI?

options.name: Local evaluators for tool calls and keywords on every change with `num_repetitions=3`, Foundry evaluators nightly or per release
options.why: Cheap deterministic checks gate every change, repetitions expose non-determinism, and judged scores run where cost is acceptable.
options.tradeoff: Local checks are shallow, and judged scores have their own bias and cost.

options.name: Foundry judge evaluators on every commit
options.tradeoff: Slower and costlier per commit, with judge noise.

options.name: Manual spot checks
options.tradeoff: Fine for exploration before a test set exists.

flips.if: Tool-call correctness is the main risk
flips.then: Use `tool_calls_present` and `tool_call_args_match` with expected tool calls.

flips.if: The agent is a multi-agent workflow

scenarios.takeaway: Put cheap deterministic checks in the inner loop and judged metrics at the gate.

quiz.q: Which statements about Python telemetry defaults are true? Select all.
options: Instrumentation has been on by default since python-1.6.0 (2026-05-21)
Sensitive data means prompts, responses, tool arguments and tool results
quiz.explain: Sensitive data capture defaults to false, and nothing is exported until you configure an exporter.

quiz.q: Your Python agent emits spans to a local collector, but a Langfuse backend receives nothing. What is the most likely cause?
options: Langfuse accepts OTLP over HTTP, while the Python default exporter protocol is gRPC
quiz.explain: Langfuse takes OTLP over HTTP JSON or protobuf, not gRPC. Set the OTLP protocol to `http/protobuf`.

quiz.q: You need MCP server spans to be children of the agent span. Which tool setup achieves it in Python?
options: Any MCP tool, as injection is automatic everywhere
quiz.explain: The framework injects trace context only for MCP sessions the agent process opens. Provider-issued calls bypass it.

flashcards.front: Name the three core Agent Framework span names.
How do you enable .NET agent telemetry, and which source name must you add?
flashcards.back: `.AsBuilder().UseOpenTelemetry(sourceName, ...)` on the client or agent. Default source `Experimental.Microsoft.Agents.AI`; `AddSource` must match.

flashcards.front: What are the Python evaluation entry points?
flashcards.back: `evaluate_agent()` and `evaluate_workflow()` with `LocalEvaluator`, `@evaluator` checks and `FoundryEvals`; `num_repetitions` measures consistency.
